items.stem: Why does a model card include 'out-of-scope uses' and not only intended uses?

options.text: It warns against foreseeable misuse the evaluation does not support, reducing harm from over-generalisation
options.rationale: Correct: out-of-scope statements guard against unsupported misuse.

options.text: To make the document longer for auditors
options.rationale: It serves a safety purpose, not length.
Intended uses are still required; out-of-scope complements them.

options.text: To transfer all liability to the user
options.rationale: A disclaimer does not transfer accountability; it informs use.

items.explanation: Correct: out-of-scope statements guard against unsupported misuse.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO items most belong in a model card? (Select TWO.)

options.text: The evaluation data and metrics, with their conditions
options.rationale: Correct: evaluation details are core model-card content.

options.text: Known limitations and conditions under which performance degrades
options.rationale: Correct: limitations are core model-card content.

options.text: The marketing tagline for the product
options.rationale: Marketing copy is not model documentation.

items.explanation: Correct: evaluation details are core model-card content.

items.stem: A model is replaced by a better version but the old one still serves some traffic unnoticed. Which governance control was missing?

options.text: A model inventory with versioning and a retirement trigger
options.rationale: Correct: inventory and retirement controls prevent orphaned models in production.
Dataset size does not prevent orphaned deployments.
Documentation length does not retire a model.

items.explanation: Correct: inventory and retirement controls prevent orphaned models in production.
